title: SECOND BELL — Collaborative learning furniture from reclaimed school desk frames, 6 deliverables

config.text:
# SECOND BELL

## Project
- Furniture: six reconfigurable learning modules using reclaimed school desk frames.
- Users: six teenagers and a session facilitator.
- Activities: independent work, paired discussion, handwork and temporary classes.
- Project wording: SECOND BELL.
- Supporting wording: Built from six school desks.

## Existing frames
- Stock: six matching frames, F01–F06.
- Overall dimensions per frame: 600 mm wide × 450 mm deep × 700 mm high.
- Material: welded 25 × 25 mm square steel tube.
- Construction: rectangular top ring, four vertical legs and one rear horizontal stretcher.
- Top ring: outer dimensions 600 × 450 mm; vertical extent 675–700 mm above floor.
- Legs: outer faces flush with the top ring; upper ends at 675 mm above floor.
- Rear stretcher: between the rear legs, centreline 250 mm above floor.
- Welded connections per frame: four top-ring corners, four leg-to-ring joints and two rear-stretcher ends; total 10.
- Retained geometry: all tube lengths and all 10 welded connections per frame.
- Existing appearance: grey-green paint, exposed steel at worn edges and local surface rust near the feet.
- Steel finish: local rust removal and a clear water-based protective finish, with existing paint and wear retained.

## Added kit
| Component | Quantity | Dimensions or construction |
|---|---:|---|
| Birch plywood top | 6 | 660 × 500 × 18 mm; corner radius 20 mm |
| Under-top birch plywood tray | 6 | External 300 × 200 × 70 mm; walls and base 9 mm; clear interior 282 × 182 × 61 mm |
| Padded split-clamp assembly | 24 | Four per top; hand-operated frame attachment |
| Removable bridge coupler | 6 | Maximum envelope per coupler 120 × 60 × 35 mm; hand-operated; two per discussion pair |
- Plywood finish: clear water-based varnish.
- Finished working height: 718 mm.
- Tray attachment location: underside of the added tabletop.
- Detached coupler allocation: two couplers per tray in three trays.
- Clamp and tray assembly hardware: part of the corresponding assembly.

## Space and states
- Room: clear rectangle 6000 × 4800 mm.
- Plan orientation: access from the bottom edge.
- Continuous circulation route: minimum clear width 900 mm.
- Independent work: six separate workstations; six detached couplers in trays.
- Discussion: three face-to-face pairs; two fitted bridge couplers per pair.
- Storage: six complete modules within a 2100 × 1100 mm floor area; six detached couplers in three trays.
- Component inventory across states: six frames, six tops, six trays, 24 frame-clamp assemblies and six bridge couplers.

steps.userMessage:
SECOND BELL | Collaborative learning furniture from reclaimed school desk frames

Our community learning room needs furniture for six teenagers to work individually, gather in pairs for discussion and handwork, and clear the centre for a temporary class. Develop SECOND BELL around our six matching school desk frames, F01–F06. Each welded steel frame measures 600 mm wide × 450 mm deep × 700 mm high and uses 25 × 25 mm square tube. Retain every tube at its existing length and all 10 welded connections on each frame. The grey-green paint and local wear are part of the furniture's identity; use local rust removal and a clear water-based protective finish on the steel.

The added kit comprises six 660 × 500 × 18 mm birch plywood tops with 20 mm corner radii, six under-top birch plywood trays, 24 padded split-clamp assemblies attaching the tops to the frames, and six removable bridge couplers joining adjacent tops. Finish the plywood with clear water-based varnish. Each tray has external dimensions of 300 × 200 × 70 mm and 9 mm walls and base. Each bridge coupler fits within 120 × 60 × 35 mm and operates by hand, as do the frame clamps. Use two couplers per discussion pair; all six couplers have a place in the trays when detached. The room provides a clear 6000 × 4800 mm rectangle. The stored furniture must fit within a 2100 × 1100 mm floor area. Print "SECOND BELL" and "Built from six school desks" on the assembly sheet and both detail sheets.

Audience: the community room coordinator, teenage participants and the fabrication workshop, for choosing the working arrangement and preparing the furniture for fabrication.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records the fixed dimensions, materials, kit quantities and operating states. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables with their proportions, formats and stages. 03-frame-register.en.md records the six frame IDs and retained connections. frame-dimensions.png provides measured frame geometry, weld locations and stock quantity. school-desk-frame.png establishes the existing frame's recognisable construction, paint and wear. learning-room-atmosphere.png provides the social atmosphere of individual work, paired discussion and a cleared teaching space.

Deliverables:
1. One final assembly sheet with an exploded view of one complete module, a six-module parts schedule, frame IDs F01–F06, and the relationship between retained steel and added components
2. One independent-work layout with a dimensioned room plan and an occupied view of six separate workstations
3. One discussion layout with a dimensioned room plan and an occupied view of three face-to-face pairs, each joined by two bridge couplers
4. One storage layout with a dimensioned plan and an overall view of all six modules inside the 2100 × 1100 mm storage area, including the locations of detached couplers
5. One tabletop and connection detail sheet with dimensioned sections through the 18 mm top, padded frame clamp and removable bridge coupler, plus the hand-operated release sequence
6. One under-top storage detail sheet with dimensioned tray construction, its attachment to the tabletop, and the arrangement of two detached bridge couplers inside one tray

Acceptance:
- The assembly sheet accounts for F01–F06 and totals six retained frames, six tops, six trays, 24 padded split-clamp assemblies and six bridge couplers; its exploded view identifies the retained tubes and all 10 welded connections per frame.
- The independent-work, discussion and storage layouts each account for the same six frames, tops and trays and all six bridge couplers. The independent layout seats six people separately; the discussion layout seats six people in three face-to-face pairs with two couplers per pair.
- The three layout sheets dimension the 6000 × 4800 mm room and a continuous clear route at least 900 mm wide from the bottom edge of the plan to every occupied workstation or the stored group. The storage layout dimensions the complete furniture footprint within 2100 × 1100 mm.
- The tabletop and connection detail sheet dimensions the 660 × 500 × 18 mm top, 20 mm corner radii, 718 mm finished working height and each coupler's maximum 120 × 60 × 35 mm envelope; its sections and release sequence explain four padded frame clamps per module and hand operation of both connection types.
- The storage detail sheet dimensions the 300 × 200 × 70 mm tray, its 9 mm walls and base, and its tabletop attachment. Its packed view accommodates two detached couplers; the storage layout locates the full set of six couplers in three trays.
- The assembly sheet and both detail sheets print SECOND BELL and Built from six school desks. Their material labels specify birch plywood with clear water-based varnish and retained steel with local rust removal and a clear water-based protective finish; the occupied and storage views carry through the frame's grey-green paint and visible wear.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
